title: Simplicity conjecture for the homotopy eigenvalues
statement:
Let ${{\boldsymbol{M}}}_n$ and ${\boldsymbol{S}}_n$ be the matrices described above, and define

$$
{\boldsymbol{T}}({\varepsilon}) = \begin{bmatrix}
 {\varepsilon}{\boldsymbol{e}}_1{\boldsymbol{e}}_1^T & 0 & {\boldsymbol{S}}_n\\
 0 & 0 & {\varepsilon}{\boldsymbol{e}}_1^T \\
 {\boldsymbol{S}}_n & {\varepsilon}{\boldsymbol{e}}_1 & 0
 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Here ${\boldsymbol{T}}({\varepsilon})$ is the symmetric homotopy matrix and $\varepsilon$ is the continuation parameter. **Simplicity conjecture.** The eigenvalues of ${\boldsymbol{T}}({\varepsilon})$ are simple on $0 \leq \varepsilon$.
This conjecture is motivated by numerical discriminant calculations: the calculated discriminants have strictly positive coefficients as polynomials in $\varepsilon$.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.01116

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).
source_name: Neil J. Calkin, Eunice Y. S. Chan, Robert M. Corless, David J. Jeffrey and Piers W. Lawrence, “A Fractal Eigenvector”, arXiv:2104.01116 (2021).
